content: Ferric subsulfate solution is a chemical agent that functions as a styptic or hemostatic agent, meaning it is used to control bleeding. It is commonly applied after superficial skin biopsies to stop minor bleeding. This solution is also referred to as Basic Ferric Sulfate Solution or Monsel's Solution. Its formulation is officially recognized and published in the United States Pharmacopeia 29. The active ingredients in ferric subsulfate solution are derived from ferrous sulfate, sulfuric acid, and nitric acid. Each 100 mL of the solution contains basic ferric sulfate, which is equivalent to an iron content of no less than 20 grams and no more than 22 grams. Ferric subsulfate solution must be stored in airtight containers at a temperature above 22 degrees Celsius. If the temperature drops below 22 degrees Celsius, crystallization of the solution may occur. However, warming the solution can help dissolve the crystals back into the liquid. Additionally, the solution should be protected from exposure to light to maintain its stability. One of the commercially available formulations of ferric subsulfate solution is Astringyn, produced by Cooper Surgical. This product is a thickened gel formulation that has been specially modified for ease of application and enhanced performance.
